title: Carleo & Troyer Neural-Network Quantum States Solve Strongly Correlated Many-Body Ground States and Dynamics
whyItMatters: Published in Science, Carleo & Troyer represented exponentially complex quantum many-body wavefunctions as restricted Boltzmann machines—surpassing tensor-network benchmarks on 2D spin lattices and launching neural quantum physics.
summary: Published in Science on February 10, 2017, Giuseppe Carleo and Matthias Troyer at ETH Zurich introduced Neural-Network Quantum States (NQS), using restricted Boltzmann machines (RBMs) trained via reinforcement-style variational Monte Carlo to compactly represent exponentially large quantum many-body wavefunctions. On benchmark 1D and 2D transverse-field Ising and antiferromagnetic Heisenberg models, their neural wavefunctions achieved ground-state energies and unitary time-evolution accuracy surpassing state-of-the-art tensor-network and projected entangled-pair state (PEPS) methods—directly inaugurating the neural quantum physics movement that produced FermiNet (2020) and modern neural QMC.
technicalHighlights: Represented complex quantum many-body wavefunctions using restricted Boltzmann machines with complex weights trained by variational Monte Carlo.
Outperformed leading tensor-network/PEPS baselines on 2D Heisenberg ground-state energies and captured unitary quantum quench dynamics.
Launched the entire field of Neural-Network Quantum States (NetKet, FermiNet, PauliNet, Psiformer).
caveats: Initial RBM ansatz struggled with non-stoquastic fermionic sign structures before antisymmetric neural wavefunctions (FermiNet, PauliNet) in 2020.

scoreRationale.foundational: Created the neural-wavefunction paradigm for tackling the exponential Hilbert-space curse in quantum many-body physics.
scoreRationale.ripple: Cited >4,000 times and directly enabled FermiNet, PauliNet, and modern neural quantum Monte Carlo.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Science (Vol. 355, pp. 602–606) with exact variational energy bounds verified against QMC and DMRG.
scoreRationale.velocity: Dramatically expanded tractable 2D quantum many-body ground-state and dynamical simulations.
